title: A categorical and algebro-geometric theory of localization — Proposition 4.13
author: Mauricio Corr\^ea, Simone Noja
work: A categorical and algebro-geometric theory of localization
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition 4.13 (source0.tex lines 653--667, source label prop:Loc-excision), the excision statement for the localisation torsors of the paper's categorical localisation theory: if v: V -> X is an open neighbourhood of a closed Z with induced maps i_V and j_V, if the base-change square satisfies the recollement hypotheses and a class c vanishes on the open complement, then the localisation torsor of c on X agrees with the localisation torsor of v*c on V, with the two sides simultaneously singletons. The complete original proof (source0.tex lines 669--709, 41 adjacent lines) is a genuine research-level argument in a six-functor formalism: it manipulates the canonical identification of Hom-groups through the base-change isomorphisms, constructs the comparison of torsors from the recollement data, and checks the singleton statement on both sides. H2: a complete original research-paper proposition with a fully written proof of moderate length whose steps are nontrivial six-functor and torsor constructions rather than routine verifications.
